_note: What the head coach says in his own words (GDD 4.9.2, session C3; read by CoachTalk, scripts/core/coach_talk.gd). Three uses: (1) the Sunday-evening WEEK TALK (last week in a few lines from the day log, this week explained from the season plan: phase, why the key sessions, one thing to focus on; it always stops Play week, user 2026-10-11), (2) the MESSAGE after a race (the facts, the coach's Race-story line in his own words from coaches.json, a closing line), (3) the coach's WHY line in the day editor. His COMMUNICATION attribute sets the detail (detail.short_max / full_min: short = 'Do it.', normal, full = he explains why); his personality (coaches.json voice: calm / drill / warm / tactician) sets the voice. Placeholders in a text are filled by the code: {name} (the athlete's first name), {coach_first}, {done}, {planned}, {n}, {meet}, {result}, {phase}, {week}, {weeks}, {weekday}, {session}, {why}, {short}, {areas}, {area}, {injury}, {days}. Topics (the 0-2 questions with replies) are storylets in data/storylets/week_talk.json. Texts only here, never in scripts.

scratched._note: Session F1 (playtest 2: 'a niggle before the race, I skipped it, the coach said nothing before or after'): the head coach's message in his thread when the player scratches from an entered race (Game.scratch_race; not when it was his own advice: he has answered that already). hurt = an injury or a sore area today; school = scratched for a busy test week; plain = no reason he can see. {meet} = the meet, {area} = the most loaded body area, {next} = the next entered race's line (next / no_next). The line is picked by the meet (no dice).
hurt: Good call on {meet}. Racing on sore {area} can cost you weeks; one race costs nothing.
Right decision. {meet} isn't worth your {area}. We let it settle first.

phase_why.general_base: This phase builds the engine. The training is easy on purpose: it makes everything later possible.
phase_why.indoor_specific: The indoor target is close, so we add race-pace work and sharpen up.
phase_why.spring_base: Back to building before the outdoor season: tempo, hills and strength.
phase_why.pre_competition: Racing is near. Speed work now makes the first outdoor races sharp.
phase_why.race_season: Racing season. We keep the speed, race, and recover well in between.
phase_why.transition: Easy weeks to rest the body and the mind after the summer.
phase_why.autumn_general: A gentle start to the new training year.

easy_run.why: Easy running builds your aerobic base without tiring you. Keep it relaxed.

long_run.why: A long run teaches your body to keep going. Keep the pace easy.

fartlek.why: Fartlek mixes fast and slow running. It builds speed and stamina without a strict watch.

tempo_run.why: A tempo run at steady hard effort raises the pace you can hold.

intervals_800.why: Intervals at race pace teach your body the 800 m. Keep the reps even.

speed_strides.why: Short fast strides keep your legs quick without tiring you.

hill_sprints.why: Hill sprints build power and speed. Short and hard, with full rests.

start_practice.why: Start practice makes the first 100 metres automatic.

club_session.why: The group session pushes you with others. Run with them, not ahead of them.

strength.why: Strength and core work makes you robust and your stride stronger.

drills.why: Running drills fix your technique. Slow, precise, no rushing.

mobility.why: Mobility keeps you supple and helps you recover.

xc_skiing.why: Skiing builds your engine with little pounding on the legs.

aqua_jog.why: Running in water keeps the fitness while the legs rest.

stationary_bike.why: The bike keeps the engine going without pounding the legs.

swimming.why: Swimming is a gentle full-body session that helps you recover.

gym_core.why: Core and upper-body work keeps you strong while the legs rest.

explain.style: How the coach leads. A supportive coach asks and encourages; a controlling one tells you what to do. Neither is wrong, but some athletes need the one more than the other.
explain.demands: Which of the three season plans the coach leans towards: Steady plays it safe, Ambitious wants more.
explain.fit: How your temperament and the coach's character go together. It shows after four weeks together. You click, it is fine, or there is some friction. It moves how much you trust each other.
explain.trust: How much you trust each other. It grows when you listen to the coach and do well, and falls when you ignore the advice. A strong bond means more explaining.

verdict._note: Session C4 (GDD 4.9.2 'Ask the coach'; CoachVerdict). words = the four verdicts. reasons = why, by the part of the change that decided it as HE sees it (rest = it lowers the injury risk, fresh = better Form at the race, work = the week gives more training (a heavier day, or one that is not lighter; a LIGHTER change that gives more training says work_light instead: session F1, CoachVerdict.reason_for), race = racing is worth it, risk / form = what makes it Risky, lose_work / form_loss / bit_risky / nothing = Pointless, fine / tradeoff = Fine); short = what a coach with communication <= detail.short_max says instead, detail = the extra sentence of one with >= detail.full_min. voice = his opening word per verdict. compare = the line that says what was compared. Placeholders: {area} (the most loaded body area), {meet}, {day}, {coach_first}, {name}.

rest: Your {area} have taken a lot lately; easing off now keeps you out of trouble.
Your {area} could use the break, and it costs you very little.
fresh: It leaves your legs fresh for {meet}.
work: You'll get more out of the week this way, and your body can take it right now.
It makes the week better training, and you're fresh enough for it.
work_light: Easing off here lets the sessions that matter count for more.
You'll get more out of the hard days if this one is lighter.
race: Race it. Racing is how you learn to race.
Go and race. You're fit enough for it.
risk: Your {area} are already loaded. That's asking for an injury.
That's a lot on your {area} right now. That's how injuries start.
form: So close to {meet}, you'd race on tired legs.
That tiredness would still be in your legs at {meet}.
lose_work: You'd lose good training and gain nothing for it.
You're fresh. There's no reason to back off.
form_loss: It takes a little of your edge off for {meet}, for nothing.
bit_risky: It's a bit much for your {area}, and it doesn't give you much.
nothing: It makes no real difference either way.
tradeoff: You give up a little, you gain a little. Either way works.

short.work: More out of the week. Good.
short.lose_work: You lose a session for nothing.

detail.rest: One lighter day costs you little; an injury costs weeks.
detail.fresh: Hard work this close to a race doesn't make you fitter in time, it only makes you tired.
detail.work: The sessions that matter give you more when the week is built this way.
detail.work_light: Fitness comes from the key sessions, and they give more on fresher legs.
detail.race: The day's training would give you less than the race itself.
detail.risk: Soreness is the warning; most running injuries start when it's ignored.
detail.form: The fitness from it comes after the race; the tiredness comes right away.
detail.lose_work: Fitness comes from the sessions you do, and you can handle this one.
detail.form_loss: Keep the sharp work, ease off the volume instead.
detail.bit_risky: The extra strain is bigger than what it builds.
detail.tradeoff: If your legs feel good, train; if not, ease off.

warm.risky: Please don't, I'm worried about this.

ask._note_l3b1: Session L3b1 (the user's 'same plan, same answer'): his dice for a weekly plan come from the plan, not from the button or the date. The card says which week was judged: next_normal when next week is the phase's own week (then the phase's page gives the same answer), next_other when it is a lighter week, a taper or easing back in (judged as it is).
ask.next_normal: Next week: {week}. The phase's normal week, so the phase's page gets the same answer.
ask.next_other: Next week: {week}. {He} {v:judges|judge} it as it is, not the phase's normal week.
ask.head: {coach_first} on this
ask.note: A coach's view is only as good as the coach: a weak one can be wrong both ways.

proposal._note: Session C4 (GDD 4.9.2 'Proposals and the veto'; CoachProposals). His messages when he changes, would change or asks to change your days, and when he advises scratching. intro = per voice; {change} = the day lines ('Thursday: Easy run instead of 800 m intervals.'); {reason} = his verdict reason (verdict.reasons, in his detail); replies = the buttons of 'Ask me first' (each veto reason gets 'Veto: ' in front); answered = his reply after your answer, per voice. settings = the standing order 'Let the coach adjust my days'. ui = the day editor's texts.
